neighbours.label: retreating to a refuge: the word marking the safe place or person one withdraws to (retreat 'to', comes 'to' me when scared, flees 'home', safe 'haven')
fire: Every child needs a calm corner to withdraw to.
When thunder rattles the windows, the dog runs to me.
The cave gave the villagers somewhere safe to flee to.
During the crisis, gold was once again a safe haven for savers.
When the toddler gets overwhelmed, she crawls back to her mother.
The monastery was a sanctuary he could always retreat to.
Frightened by the fireworks, the cat fled home.
After a hard day, the garden shed is the refuge I escape to.
quiet: Every child needs a warm coat to wear in winter.
When the mail arrives, the dog barks at the door.
The cave gave the scientists many fossils to study.
During the crisis, gold was once again taxed by the state.
When the toddler gets hungry, she points to the fridge.
The monastery sent a letter to the bishop.
Amused by the fireworks, the cat watched from the window.
After a hard day, he drove to the gym.

notes: Card: ' to' x9, ' back' x6, ' home' x2, ' safe' (haven) of the top 32: 'retreat to', a Rückzugsraum, 'brings you back', 'if the pup gets scared he comes to me'. Probes: 'a quiet place to retreat to' 0.91, 'safe haven' 0.70, 'frightened it comes to me' 0.59, 'ran home to her mother' 0.33; but 'went back to the cabin' in a storm only 0.12; ordinary 'to' (walked to the store, handed the letter to) 0.01.
